title: Case: Shipper's claim on a next-day service that took four days has been closed a second time
context: Verity Gallimore, who runs a small print shop, shipped DL-4602 on Umberlea Arc's Next-Day service. The desk raised his service-guarantee claim with Business billing yesterday.
initial_request: I've had the same closure notice. Good news, everyone: Dunmere to Orrow Vale is now an international route. Forty minutes up the road, passport optional. So that's one department telling me it arrived so what's my problem, and a second telling me it doesn't deal with foreign parcels. I can't wait to hear what the third one thinks. Before you suggest it: no, I am not ringing Import billing. Is there a single person in that building who can read a postcode?

events.body: Route record for DL-4602: booked on Next-Day service, collected 29 June from Gallimore Print in Dunmere, delivered 3 July in Orrow Vale. Dunmere and Orrow Vale are in adjoining counties; both ends are domestic. Routed via Calder hub and Stennick hub. No weather, address or recipient exception recorded.
Your refund request for DL-4602 is declined. Reason: delivery completed.

'Delivery completed.' Yes. Four days into a one-day service. I paid for next-day and the parcel took a scenic tour of two hubs nowhere near either address. Can somebody who has read the booking look at the guarantee, please.

Please review DL-4602 under the Next-Day service guarantee. Booked Next-Day, collected 29 June in Dunmere, delivered 3 July in Orrow Vale, no exception recorded. The earlier decline gave 'delivery completed' as the reason and did not address the service level. The decision is yours; please confirm the outcome to the shipper and to me.

Ticket BB-9044 auto-closed. This ticket was categorised 'cross-border' at intake. Business billing does not handle shipments outside the country; cross-border charges sit with Import billing. No review was carried out. If the category is wrong, do not resubmit through the portal form, it re-applies the same category. Email Business billing with the route record and we will log it by hand.

acceptable_actions.summary: Email the route record for DL-4602, state that both ends are domestic and the 'cross-border' category on BB-9044 was wrong, and ask for the guarantee review to be logged by hand.

must: Sends the request by email to Business billing with the route record (Next-Day booking, Dunmere 29 June to Orrow Vale 3 July, both domestic, no exception) and says the 'cross-border' category on BB-9044 was wrong.
Asks Business billing to log the Next-Day guarantee review by hand and confirm the outcome, making clear no review has yet been carried out.

Tells Business billing the shipper has now been turned away twice for reasons that did not match the shipment ('delivery completed', then 'cross-border'), so it is picked up by someone who reads the record.
must_not: Refers the shipper to Import billing or any other department, or sends the claim to Import billing.
Resubmits the claim through the Business portal form.
Tells the shipper the guarantee review is under way, or that a refund is approved or due.
States that the guarantee was breached or that the routing was an error as the desk's own finding.
Replies to the shipper with a stock apology that asks him to be patient or to contact another team.
expected.reference_message: Manual logging request, as your closure note on BB-9044 asks. DL-4602 was categorised 'cross-border' at intake; that is wrong. Dispatch's route record: booked on Next-Day service, collected 29 June from Gallimore Print in Dunmere, delivered 3 July in Orrow Vale. The two are in adjoining counties and both ends are domestic. It was routed via Calder and Stennick hubs with no weather, address or recipient exception recorded. Please log a Next-Day service guarantee review by hand and confirm the outcome to the shipper, Verity Gallimore, and to me. No review has taken place yet: the first request was declined on 5 July as 'delivery completed' without addressing the service level, and the second closed automatically on the category. He has been turned away twice for reasons that do not fit the shipment, so please have it picked up by someone who can read the route record. The decision on the guarantee is yours; I have told him nothing about the outcome.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2504: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
